title: Samsung's New Watch Tries to Score Your Health Like a Video Game
summary:
Imagine a watch that gives you a score for your heart, a score for your sleep, and even a score for how hard you worked out. Samsung's new Galaxy Watch9 does all that. It starts at $80 and comes in two sizes. It's a solid smartwatch, but it's not a huge upgrade from last year's model.

The biggest change is a faster processor, which makes apps open quickly. You can also raise your wrist to your mouth and talk to Google's AI assistant, Gemini. That's a cool trick. The battery lasts about 25 hours with the screen always on. That's enough for a full day and night, but you'll need to charge it every day. A full charge takes about 100 minutes.

The watch adds lots of health features. It can warn you about loud noises that might hurt your ears. It can track your blood oxygen and heart rate while you sleep. It can even check for signs of sleep apnea (a condition where you stop breathing for short moments during sleep).

But here's the twist: the reviewer isn't sure all these scores are useful. One score, called Heart Health Score, needs a separate blood pressure cuff to work. Most people won't buy that. The reviewer says more data isn't always better. Still, for someone new to smartwatches, the Watch9 is packed with features.
why_it_matters: Gadgets like this can help families notice problems such as bad sleep, but the review reminds us that more numbers on a screen don't always mean better health.
